description:
## Research Question
How can emgithub (https://github.com/yusanshi/emgithub) be integrated into our MkDocs Material documentation to embed live GitHub code snippets, replacing static build-time code insertion?

## Summary
Integration is feasible but involves significant trade-offs. The Manual contains **~86 code embeds** across 6 pages — 78 static ```cpp blocks (provenance lost), plus 8 unconverted LaTeX commands. The heaviest page has 47 embeds alone. Script tags pass through MkDocs markdown if formatted as block-level HTML. The main challenges are: re-mapping static blocks to their source files/lines, GitHub's tightened rate limits (May 2025), highlight.js performance at 47 embeds/page, and CSS bleed from Material's global styles.

## Scope: Full Inventory of Code Embeds

| Type | Count | Files |
|---|---|---|
| ` ```cpp ` static blocks | **78** | 5 files (What CL does in detail: 46, Scalar fields: 12, Gauge fields: 9, Under the Hood: 9, List of Functions: 2) |
| `\insertcppcode` (unconverted) | **1** | What CL does in detail.md:623 |
| `\inserttxtcode` (unconverted) | **3** | Gauge fields.md:195,201,207 |
| `\inputminted` (unconverted) | **4** | Installation.md:20,53 + Scalar fields.md:201,213 |
| ` ```bash ` blocks | **33** | 5 files — shell commands, likely not emgithub candidates |
| ` ```math ` blocks | **64** | 7 files — math, not candidates |

**Total emgithub candidates: ~86** (78 cpp + 1 insertcppcode + 3 inserttxtcode + 4 inputminted)

### Per-Page Density

| Page | cpp blocks | Other code | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| What CosmoLattice does in detail | 46 | 1 insertcppcode | **47** |
| My first model of (singlet) scalar fields | 12 | 2 inputminted | **14** |
| My first model of gauge fields | 9 | 3 inserttxtcode | **12** |
| Under the Hood: Expression Templates | 9 | 0 | **9** |
| List of Implemented Functions | 2 | 0 | **2** |
| Installation | 0 | 2 inputminted | **2** |

## Key Findings

### 1. Lost Provenance — The Main Challenge

The 78 static ` ```cpp ` blocks were converted from the original LaTeX source (`mainV2.tex` from arxiv 2102.01031), which is **not stored in the repo** — `convert_arxiv_manual.sh` downloads it at build time. The original `\insertcppcode{name}{startline}{endline}{filepath}` metadata has been baked into static blocks and **the file/line mapping is lost**.

The surrounding markdown text often names the source file (e.g., "The `main` function is located in `src/cosmolattice.cpp`") but line ranges are not preserved. Converting to emgithub requires **re-mapping each block** to its current file and line range — a manual or semi-automated matching process.

Additionally, the code was snapshotted from the version at the time of the paper. Line numbers will have shifted as the codebase evolved.

### 2. Broken LaTeX Commands

8 commands remain unconverted in the markdown and render as raw text in the HTML:
- `\inserttxtcode{...}` — 3 in gauge fields page (references `code_files/lphi4SU2U1.in`)
- `\inputminted[...]{...}{...}` — 2 in Installation (bash scripts), 2 in scalar fields (CMakeLists.txt, lphi4.in)
- `\insertcppcode{...}` — 1 in detail page (split across 2 lines, may break regex)

The converter (`default.py:50-67`) only handles `\insertcppcode`. `\inserttxtcode` and `\inputminted` have **no conversion rule** — these need fixing regardless of emgithub.

### 3. Current Build Pipeline

- `documentation/build.sh` clones the repo into `tmp/code_source/`, copies source to `website/`, runs `mkdocs build`
- `convert_arxiv_manual.sh` downloads arxiv tarball → runs `split_manual.py` → outputs markdown (currently commented out in build.sh line 17)
- `insert_code()` in `default.py:50-67` reads local files at build time, emits fenced ```cpp blocks
- Call chain: `base.py` → `default_block()` → `insert_code(lines, tmpdir)` where tmpdir = `./tmp/code_source/`

### 4. MkDocs Material Feasibility

- `md_in_html` is enabled (`mkdocs.yml:57`) but **not needed** for `<script>` tags — Python-Markdown treats `<script>` as a raw tag regardless (it's in the `raw_tags` set: `['canvas', 'math', 'option', 'pre', 'script', 'style', 'textarea']`)
- Script tags **must** be block-level (blank lines before/after) or they get escaped to `<script>`
- No sanitization of `src=` URLs occurs
- MkDocs Material maintainer recommends `extra_javascript` for external scripts, but inline block-level `<script>` tags do work

### 5. emgithub Script Tag Format

```html
<script src="https://emgithub.com/embed-v2.js?target=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fcosmolattice%2Fcosmolattice_private%2Fblob%2Fmain%2F{path}%23L{start}-L{end}&style=github&type=code&showBorder=on&showLineNumbers=on&showFileMeta=on&showCopy=on&fetchFromJsDelivr=on"></script>
```

**Parameters** (checked with `=== "on"`, any other value = off):
- `target` (required): URL-encoded GitHub blob URL with `#L{start}-L{end}` fragment
- `style`: highlight.js theme name
- `type`: `code` | `markdown` | `ipynb`
- `showBorder`, `showLineNumbers`, `showFileMeta`, `showFullPath`, `showCopy`: `on` | omit
- `fetchFromJsDelivr`: `on` | omit — use jsDelivr CDN instead of raw.githubusercontent.com
- `maxHeight`: integer pixels
- `ts`: integer (tab width)

Line ranges specified via GitHub URL fragment: `#L80-L92` (URL-encoded as `%23L80-L92`).

### 6. Mapping Local Paths → emgithub URLs

For the `\insertcppcode`/`\inserttxtcode` commands that still have metadata:
- `\insertcppcode{name}{startline}{endline}{filepath}`
- `name` = repo-relative path (e.g., `src/include/CosmoInterface/definitions/gaugederivatives.h`)
- GitHub URL: `https://github.com/cosmolattice/cosmolattice_private/blob/main/{name}#L{startline}-L{endline}`
- Must be URL-encoded for the `target` parameter

For the 78 static blocks: provenance must be reconstructed by matching code content against repo files.

### 7. CSS Conflicts

- **Pygments** (Material build-time): `<div class="highlight">` with `.highlight .k`, `.highlight .s` classes
- **highlight.js** (emgithub runtime): `<code class="hljs">` with `.hljs-keyword`, `.hljs-string` classes
- **No direct class collision** due to different prefixes
- **Real risks**:
  - Material's global `pre > code` CSS (background, padding, font) bleeds into emgithub containers
  - If `hljs.highlightAll()` fires, it corrupts Pygments-highlighted blocks on the same page
  - highlight.js theme CSS may include global `code { background: ... }` resets
  - Material's code annotations/copy/line-highlighting features are incompatible with hljs blocks
- **Mitigations**: CSS scoping overrides in `extra.css`, or iframe mode (full isolation, higher overhead)

### 8. Performance: 47 Embeds on One Page

emgithub's highlight.js race condition (issue #40, open, help wanted): each `<script>` tag independently checks `if (typeof hljs === 'undefined')` before injecting highlight.js. On fast connections, multiple embeds all inject it before any load completes → N redundant downloads (~50-70 KB each).

With **47 embeds** on "What CosmoLattice does in detail", this is a **critical performance concern**.

**Workarounds**:
- Pre-load highlight.js globally via `extra_javascript` in `mkdocs.yml` before any embeds execute. emgithub's conditional logic will detect `hljs` and skip injection.
- Use iframe embedding mode — each iframe is isolated (but higher per-frame overhead).

### 9. Rate Limits (May 2025)

- GitHub tightened `raw.githubusercontent.com` limits — community reports ~1 req/min/IP for unauthenticated (down from ~83/min). Exact thresholds undisclosed.
- No auth possible on raw.githubusercontent.com (tokens silently ignored, no rate-limit headers returned)
- 429 error: "Access has been restricted. You have triggered a rate limit."
- Per public IP — all tools on same machine share the bucket

With 47 embeds loading on a single page, every visitor would fire 47 requests to raw.githubusercontent.com — **guaranteed rate limiting**.

### 10. jsDelivr CDN (`fetchFromJsDelivr=on`)

- URL: `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/{user}/{repo}@{branch}/{filePath}`
- Removes rate-limit risk entirely
- **But**: files cached permanently on first access. Updates not reflected without manual purge via jsDelivr API.
- `@branch` URLs may resolve inconsistently across edge nodes
- emgithub README warns: "could be faster but may experience the cache issue"
- **Contradicts the "live current state" goal** — readers may see stale code

### 11. Self-Hosting emgithub

- Fully static site — fork, delete CNAME, enable GitHub Pages
- Critical: 404s must serve `404.html` (URL-rewriting trick). Nginx: `try_files $uri /404.html;`
- Cannot share GitHub Pages with MkDocs docs (both need 404/root routing)
- Cleanest: separate repo at `cosmolattice.github.io/emgithub-self`
- Gives full control over fetching mechanism — could bypass both rate limits and cache staleness

### 12. Styling

Best theme matches for white primary / light-blue accent Material theme:
- `github` — closest to GitHub's own look, neutral white
- `atom-one-light` — warm off-white, balanced
- `vs` — very white, understated
- `base16/google-light` — Material-adjacent palette
- `stackoverflow-light` — familiar developer look

emgithub has ~94 light themes total in its `lightStyles` array.

### 13. Fallback / Offline Strategy

- `offline` plugin is enabled in `mkdocs.yml:49` — emgithub embeds will be **blank offline**
- emgithub content is **not indexed** by MkDocs search
- Options:
  - Keep static code blocks alongside emgithub (dual output: `<noscript>` or collapsible)
  - Wrap static block in `<details>` as "static version" fallback
  - At 86 embeds, maintaining dual output is more work but preserves search/offline

## Code References

- `documentation/scripts/util/default.py:50-67` — `insert_code()` function
- `documentation/scripts/util/default.py:154-168` — `default_block()` (calls insert_code)
- `documentation/scripts/base.py` — imports and calls default_block
- `documentation/build.sh` — build pipeline (clones repo, runs mkdocs)
- `documentation/convert_arxiv_manual.sh` — downloads arxiv source, runs split_manual.py
- `documentation/source/mkdocs.yml:57` — md_in_html enabled
- `documentation/source/mkdocs.yml:49` — offline plugin enabled
- `documentation/source/mkdocs.yml:59-63` — pymdownx.highlight config (Pygments)
- `documentation/source/docs/extra.css` — currently only MathJax sizing (`.MathJax { font-size: 1.1em }`)

### Files with code embeds
- `documentation/source/docs/Manual/What CosmoLattice does in detail.md` — 47 embeds
- `documentation/source/docs/Manual/My first model of (singlet) scalar fields.md` — 14 embeds
- `documentation/source/docs/Manual/My first model of gauge fields.md` — 12 embeds
- `documentation/source/docs/Manual/Under the Hood: Expression Templates and CosmoLattice.md` — 9 embeds
- `documentation/source/docs/Manual/List of Implemented Functions.md` — 2 embeds
- `documentation/source/docs/Manual/Installation.md` — 2 embeds

## Design Options

**Option A — Modify build pipeline**: Extend `insert_code()` in `default.py` to emit emgithub `<script>` tags instead of (or alongside) static blocks. Requires adding `\inserttxtcode` and `\inputminted` handlers too. Only works for the 8 commands that still have metadata. The 78 static blocks need separate handling.

**Option B — Re-map all 86 blocks**: Match each static code block's content against current repo files to recover file paths and line ranges. Replace with emgithub tags. Pre-load highlight.js globally to avoid the race condition. Use `fetchFromJsDelivr=on` or self-host. Keep static blocks as `<noscript>` fallback.

**Option C — Self-host with custom fetcher**: Fork emgithub, modify the fetch mechanism to use GitHub API (authenticated, higher limits) or a caching proxy. Deploy on separate GitHub Pages. Eliminates both rate limits and cache staleness.

## Open Questions

- Will the repo remain at `cosmolattice/cosmolattice_private` or be renamed when made public?
- How important is offline support? (the `offline` plugin is enabled)
- Should bash/shell blocks also become live embeds, or only C++ and config files?
- Is it acceptable for line ranges to drift as the code evolves, or should embeds reference a tagged release?
- How much code drift has occurred since the arxiv paper — are the 78 static snippets still accurate to current source?

## Detailed Web Research Notes

### emgithub Script Tag — Full Parameter Reference
All parameters checked with `=== "on"` (any other value = off):
- `target` (required): URL-encoded GitHub blob URL with optional `#L{start}-L{end}` fragment
- `style`: highlight.js theme name (default varies)
- `type`: `code` | `markdown` | `ipynb`
- `showBorder`: `on` | omit
- `showLineNumbers`: `on` | omit
- `showFileMeta`: `on` | omit (file metadata footer)
- `showFullPath`: `on` | omit
- `showCopy`: `on` | omit
- `fetchFromJsDelivr`: `on` | omit
- `maxHeight`: integer pixels
- `ts`: integer (tab width)

### Light Themes Suitable for CosmoLattice Docs
~94 light themes in emgithub's `lightStyles` array. Best matches for white/light-blue:
- `github` — closest to GitHub's own look
- `atom-one-light` — warm off-white, balanced
- `vs` — very white, understated
- `base16/google-light` — Material-adjacent palette
- `stackoverflow-light` — familiar developer look
- `base16/cupertino` — macOS-inspired

### Rate Limits Deep Dive (May 2025)
- GitHub Changelog May 8, 2025: "Updated rate limits for unauthenticated requests"
- Covers raw.githubusercontent.com, HTTPS cloning, anonymous REST API
- Exact thresholds not publicly disclosed
- Community reports: ~1 unauthenticated req/min/IP (down from ~83/min)
- No auth headers accepted on raw.githubusercontent.com (silently ignored)
- No rate-limit response headers returned
- 429 error: "Access has been restricted. You have triggered a rate limit."
- Per public IP — all tools on same machine share the bucket
- Authenticated alternative: GitHub REST API `/repos/:owner/:repo/contents/:path`
- With 47 embeds on one page, every visitor fires 47 requests — guaranteed rate limiting without jsDelivr or self-hosting

### jsDelivr as CDN
- URL format: `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/{user}/{repo}@{branch}/{filePath}`
- Files cached permanently on first access — even if source deleted
- Cache invalidation requires jsDelivr purge API
- `@latest` / `@branch` URLs may resolve inconsistently across edge nodes
- January 2025 incident: cached lists outdated for several days
- emgithub README warns: "could be faster but may experience the cache issue"
- Contradicts the goal of showing "live current state" of code

### Self-Hosting Details
- Fork repo → delete CNAME file → enable GitHub Pages
- Critical: 404s must serve 404.html (URL-rewriting trick)
- Nginx: `try_files $uri /404.html;`
- Cannot share GitHub Pages with MkDocs (both need 404/root routing control)
- Cleanest: separate repo at `{org}.github.io/emgithub-self`
- Could modify fetch mechanism for authenticated GitHub API access

### highlight.js Race Condition (Issue #40)
- Multiple `<script>` tags each check `if (typeof hljs === 'undefined')`
- If all run before first hljs loads → N redundant hljs downloads (~50-70 KB each)
- With 47 embeds on one page: potentially 47 redundant hljs loads
- Proposed fix: check DOM for existing hljs script tag instead of variable
- Status: open, help wanted, not merged
- Workaround: pre-load hljs globally via extra_javascript before embeds execute — emgithub detects existing hljs and skips injection

### MkDocs Script Tag Processing
- Python-Markdown raw_tags: `['canvas', 'math', 'option', 'pre', 'script', 'style', 'textarea']`
- Script tags passed through as-is (not processed as markdown, not sanitized)
- MUST be block-level (own line, blank lines around) or gets escaped to <script>
- `md_in_html` extension not needed for script tags specifically
- MkDocs Material maintainer recommends `extra_javascript` for external scripts

### CSS Conflict Analysis
- Pygments: `<div class="highlight">` with `.highlight .k`, `.highlight .s` etc.
- highlight.js: `<code class="hljs">` with `.hljs-keyword`, `.hljs-string` etc.
- No class name collision due to different prefixes
- Risk: Material's `pre > code` global styles bleed into emgithub containers
- Risk: `hljs.highlightAll()` could re-highlight Pygments blocks
- Risk: highlight.js theme CSS may have global `code { background: ... }` resets
- Material code annotations/copy/line-highlighting incompatible with hljs blocks
- Mitigation: iframe mode eliminates all conflicts (at iframe overhead cost)
- Mitigation: CSS scoping in extra.css to isolate emgithub containers

### Sources
- https://github.com/yusanshi/emgithub
- https://github.com/yusanshi/emgithub/blob/master/embed-v2.js
- https://github.com/yusanshi/emgithub/issues/40

## Overview
Run the lphi4SU2U1 model with three evolvers (LF, VV2, RK2) to verify the toSU2→exp() fix produces correct Gauss constraint preservation and energy conservation, using RK2 (which already used exp()) as the reference.

## Current State
The code change (cosmolattice_private-60v.1) is applied but not yet verified by simulation. The existing `models/parameter-files/lphi4SU2U1.in` provides a working parameter set.

## Desired End State
LF and VV2 Gauss constraint violation (`average_gauss_SU2_0.txt` column 2) and energy conservation (`average_energy_conservation.txt`) are comparable to or better than the old code, and do not show unbounded drift. RK2 serves as the gold-standard reference.

## What We're NOT Doing
- Testing higher-order VV (VV4, VV6, etc.)
- Regression testing against the old (pre-fix) code — we compare against RK2 instead
- Performance benchmarking

## Approach
1. Create three parameter files from the existing lphi4SU2U1.in — one per evolver (LF, VV2, RK2), outputting to separate directories
2. Build with -DMODEL=lphi4SU2U1
3. Run all three simulations
4. Compare Gauss violation and energy conservation across the three runs
title: Verify SU(2) drift fix: lphi4SU2U1 with LF/VV2/RK2

Build CosmoLattice with `-DMODEL=lphi4SU2U1` and run all three simulations (LF, VV2, RK2).

- Build succeeds without errors
- All three runs complete (exit code 0)

description:
## Overview
Compare Gauss constraint violation and energy conservation across LF, VV2, and RK2 runs to verify the fix.

## Changes Required

### 1. Compare Gauss constraint violation
Inspect `average_gauss_SU2_0.txt` from each run. Column 2 is `var(LHS-RHS)/var(LHS+RHS)` — the relative Gauss violation. It should:
- Stay bounded (not grow without limit over time)
- Be at machine precision level (~1e-14 to 1e-12) for a symplectic integrator

### 2. Compare energy conservation
Inspect `average_energy_conservation.txt` from each run. The relative Friedmann constraint violation should:
- Stay bounded
- LF and VV2 should be comparable quality to RK2

### 3. Sanity check
If LF or VV2 show significantly worse Gauss/energy preservation than RK2, investigate whether the fix introduced a regression.

## Acceptance Criteria

Manual:
- LF Gauss violation is bounded and does not grow secularly
- VV2 Gauss violation is bounded and does not grow secularly  
- LF and VV2 energy conservation is comparable to RK2
- No NaN or Inf values in any output
title: Phase 3: Compare Gauss and energy conservation across evolvers

description:
## Overview
Integrate emgithub into CosmoLattice's MkDocs Material documentation to replace static code blocks with live GitHub-sourced embeds via jsDelivr CDN. This ensures documentation always reflects the current state of the codebase.

## Current State
- ~75 code embeds across 6 Manual pages (67 static ```cpp blocks + 8 unconverted LaTeX commands)
- Provenance lost for the 67 static blocks (converted from LaTeX, file/line metadata baked in)
- Surrounding prose usually names the source file, enabling semi-automated re-mapping
- Build pipeline conversion step is commented out — markdown files are static in source/
- 8 LaTeX commands (\insertcppcode, \inserttxtcode, \inputminted) retain their metadata

## Desired End State
- All ~75 code snippets rendered via emgithub script tags pulling from GitHub via jsDelivr
- highlight.js pre-loaded globally to avoid race condition (issue #40)
- CSS isolation preventing Material theme bleed into emgithub containers
- Line drift detection tool planned for CI

## What We're NOT Doing
- Self-hosting emgithub (jsDelivr is acceptable)
- Offline fallback (acceptable to break offline)
- Converting bash or math blocks
- Changing the repo URL (stays cosmolattice/cosmolattice_private)

## Approach
1. Infrastructure: hljs preload, CSS isolation, single-embed verification
2. Pilot: Convert "Under the Hood: Expression Templates" (9 embeds)
3. Full rollout: Convert remaining 5 pages
4. Future: Line drift detection tool for CI
title: emgithub Integration into MkDocs Documentation

## Overview
Pre-load highlight.js globally so emgithub's per-embed conditional injection (`if (typeof hljs === 'undefined')`) detects it and skips redundant downloads. Without this, pages with many embeds would each independently inject hljs (~50-70KB each).

## Changes Required

### 1. mkdocs.yml — extra_javascript
**File**: `documentation/source/mkdocs.yml`
**Changes**: Add highlight.js CDN + C++ language pack to `extra_javascript` section (before any emgithub embeds execute). Use the same CDN version emgithub uses internally.

```yaml
extra_javascript:
  - javascripts/mathjax.js
  - https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/highlight.js/11.9.0/highlight.min.js
  - https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/highlight.js/11.9.0/languages/cpp.min.js
  - https://polyfill.io/v3/polyfill.min.js?features=es6
  - https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mathjax@3/es5/tex-mml-chtml.js
```

### 2. Theme CSS for highlight.js
**File**: `documentation/source/mkdocs.yml`
**Changes**: Add the `github` highlight.js theme stylesheet to `extra_css`:

```yaml
extra_css:
  - extra.css
  - https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/highlight.js/11.9.0/styles/github.min.css
```

## Acceptance Criteria

Automated:
- `mkdocs build` succeeds without errors
- Built HTML includes highlight.js script tags in `<head>`

Manual:
- Open built site in browser, confirm `hljs` is defined in console (`typeof hljs !== 'undefined'`)
- Confirm no visual regression on existing code blocks (Pygments blocks unaffected)

description:
## Research Question
In the non-RK evolvers (LeapFrog, VelocityVerlet), the SU(2) gauge link drift uses `toSU2` (Cayley-Klein projection) instead of the proper exponential map. Identify all places that need modification to replace with `exp()`.

## Summary
The two non-RK evolvers use `toSU2()` — a Cayley-Klein parametrization that sets `c0 = sqrt(1 - |v|^2)` — instead of the true SU(2) exponential map `exp()` which computes `c0 = cos|v|, ci = vi*sin|v|/|v|`. The `toSU2`-squared trick partially compensates but still introduces O(dt^2) error in the vector components and fails catastrophically when `|v|^2 >= 1`. The RK2NStorage evolver already uses the correct `exp()`. Only two methods in two files need modification.

## Key Findings

### Current (incorrect) pattern — `toSU2` with squaring trick

**LeapFrog** `driftSU2Vector` at `include/CosmoInterface/evolvers/leapfrog.h:209-218`:
```cpp
auto rescaledPi = MakeVector(
    i, 1, Model::NDim,
    toSU2(0.5 * pow(model.aSI, model.alpha - 1) * model.dx * model.dt
          * model.gQ_SU2DblSU2(0_c, n) * model.piSU2(n)(i)));
model.fldSU2(n) = (rescaledPi * rescaledPi) * model.fldSU2(n);
```

**VelocityVerlet** `driftSU2Vector` at `include/CosmoInterface/evolvers/velocityverlet.h:206-213`:
```cpp
auto rescaledPi = MakeVector(
    i, 1, Model::NDim,
    toSU2(w / 2.0 * pow(model.aSI, model.alpha - 1) * model.dx * model.dt
          * model.gQ_SU2DblSU2(0_c, n) * model.piSU2(n)(i)));
model.fldSU2(n) = (rescaledPi * rescaledPi) * model.fldSU2(n);
```

### Correct pattern — `exp()` (already used by RK2NStorage)

**RK2NStorage** `advance` for SU(2) at `include/CosmoInterface/evolvers/rk2nstorage.h:127-130`:
```cpp
ForLoop(j, 1, Model::NDim,
    model.fldSU2(n)(j) = exp(Bs[i] * Delta->fldSU2(n)(j)) * model.fldSU2(n)(j););
```

### What `toSU2` does vs `exp`

- `toSU2(v)`: `(sqrt(1 - v1^2 - v2^2 - v3^2), v1, v2, v3)` — Cayley-Klein projection
- `exp(v)`: `(cos|v|, v1*sinc|v|, v2*sinc|v|, v3*sinc|v|)` — true exponential map

Both live in `build/_deps/templat-src/include/TempLat/lattice/algebra/su2algebra/`:
- `toSU2`: `su2groupwrapper.h:100`
- `exp`: `su2expmap.h` via `SU2ExpMap` class

### Why `toSU2`-squared is not accurate enough

The squaring trick computes `V = toSU2(epsilon/2 * pi)` then applies `V^2 * U`. The quaternion square gives:
- Component 0: `1 - |v|^2/2` vs `cos|v| = 1 - |v|^2/2 + O(|v|^4)` — agree to O(|v|^2)
- Component k: `sqrt(1 - |v|^2/4) * vk = (1 - |v|^2/8 + ...) * vk` vs `sinc(|v|) * vk = (1 - |v|^2/6 + ...) * vk` — **differ at O(|v|^2)**

Additionally, `toSU2` produces NaN when `|v|^2 >= 1`, while `exp()` is well-defined everywhere.

### Required changes

**LeapFrog** (`leapfrog.h:209-218`) — replace with:
```cpp
auto rescaledPi = MakeVector(
    i, 1, Model::NDim,
    exp(pow(model.aSI, model.alpha - 1) * model.dx * model.dt
        * model.gQ_SU2DblSU2(0_c, n) * model.piSU2(n)(i)));
model.fldSU2(n) = rescaledPi * model.fldSU2(n);
```

**VelocityVerlet** (`velocityverlet.h:206-213`) — replace with:
```cpp
auto rescaledPi = MakeVector(
    i, 1, Model::NDim,
    exp(w * pow(model.aSI, model.alpha - 1) * model.dx * model.dt
        * model.gQ_SU2DblSU2(0_c, n) * model.piSU2(n)(i)));
model.fldSU2(n) = rescaledPi * model.fldSU2(n);
```

Changes: remove `/2` factor, replace `toSU2(...)` with `exp(...)`, single multiplication instead of squaring.

### No include changes needed

Both evolvers already have transitive access to `exp()` via: `kernels.h -> su2kernels.h -> kernelstypes.h -> su2algebra.h -> su2expmap.h`.

### Scope

`toSU2` is only used in these two evolver files within the project's `include/` directory (confirmed by grep). No other code paths affected.

## Code References
- `include/CosmoInterface/evolvers/leapfrog.h:209-218` — LeapFrog driftSU2Vector (needs fix)
- `include/CosmoInterface/evolvers/velocityverlet.h:206-213` — VelocityVerlet driftSU2Vector (needs fix)
- `include/CosmoInterface/evolvers/rk2nstorage.h:127-130` — RK2NStorage advance for SU(2) (reference: correct pattern)
- `build/_deps/templat-src/.../su2groupwrapper.h:100` — `toSU2` implementation
- `build/_deps/templat-src/.../su2expmap.h` — `exp()` / SU2ExpMap implementation
- `build/_deps/templat-src/.../helpers/paulivectorsalgebra.h:63-79` — expmap_inplace low-level implementation

## Open Questions
- Should the U(1) drift also be reviewed for consistency? (Currently additive, which is correct for abelian U(1))
- Are there tests/benchmarks that should be re-run to validate the change?
title: Research: Replace toSU2 with exp() in LeapFrog/VV SU(2) drift

description:
## Overview
Replace the incorrect `toSU2()` Cayley-Klein projection with the proper `exp()` exponential map in the SU(2) gauge link drift of the LeapFrog and VelocityVerlet evolvers. The RK2NStorage evolver already uses `exp()` correctly.

## Current State
Both non-RK evolvers use `toSU2(epsilon/2 * pi)` followed by squaring (`V*V*U`). This introduces O(dt^2) error in the vector components and fails when |v|^2 >= 1 (NaN from sqrt of negative).

## Desired End State
Both evolvers use `exp(epsilon * pi) * U` — the true SU(2) exponential map — matching what RK2NStorage already does. No squaring trick needed.

## What We're NOT Doing
- U(1) drift review (additive approach is correct for abelian case)
- Changes to RK2NStorage (already correct)
- Changes to TempLat library code

## Approach
Direct replacement of `toSU2(half * arg)` + squaring with `exp(full * arg)` + single multiply in both evolvers. No new includes needed — `exp()` is already transitively available.
title: Fix SU(2) drift: replace toSU2 with exp() in LeapFrog/VV

### 1. LeapFrog evolver
**File**: `include/CosmoInterface/evolvers/leapfrog.h:208-217`
**Changes**: Replace `toSU2(0.5 * ...)` + `rescaledPi * rescaledPi` with `exp(...)` + single multiply.

```cpp
    i, 1, Model::NDim,
    toSU2(0.5 * pow(model.aSI, model.alpha - 1) * model.dx * model.dt * model.gQ_SU2DblSU2(0_c, n) *
          model.piSU2(n)(i)));

// TO:

    i, 1, Model::NDim,
    exp(pow(model.aSI, model.alpha - 1) * model.dx * model.dt * model.gQ_SU2DblSU2(0_c, n) *
        model.piSU2(n)(i)));
model.fldSU2(n) = rescaledPi * model.fldSU2(n);
```

### 2. VelocityVerlet evolver
**File**: `include/CosmoInterface/evolvers/velocityverlet.h:204-213`
**Changes**: Replace `toSU2(w / 2.0 * ...)` + `rescaledPi * rescaledPi` with `exp(w * ...)` + single multiply.

```cpp
    i, 1, Model::NDim,

          model.piSU2(n)(i)));

auto rescaledPi = MakeVector(
```

## Overview
Implement a custom MkDocs hook that resolves named source-code labels into emgithub `<script>` embed tags with correct `#Lstart-Lend` line ranges. This keeps the current GitHub-style visual (file header, "View on GitHub" link, highlight.js rendering) while eliminating fragile hardcoded line numbers.

## Current State
- 14 emgithub `<script>` tags on the Scalar fields page, ~63 more across 4 other pages
- Line numbers are hardcoded — any source edit can silently break embeds
- Build clones source repos into `tmp/code_source/` (for mkdoxy); same clones can be used for label scanning
- `gen-files` plugin already runs `exclusions.py`; MkDocs hooks infrastructure is available

## Desired End State
- Source files contain label markers: `// @label:name` ... `// @endlabel`
- Docs use `@emgithub(path/to/file:label_name)` shorthand
- MkDocs hook resolves shorthand to full `<script>` tags at build time
- Rendered output is identical to current emgithub embeds
- Broken/missing labels produce visible build warnings

## What We're NOT Doing
- Converting remaining pages beyond the Scalar fields pilot (separate work)
- Addressing the public/private repo tension (future fix)
- Changing the emgithub visual style or switching to PyMdown Snippets

## Approach
1. Python label scanner module: parse `// @label:name` markers, return `{name: (start, end)}` per file
2. MkDocs `on_page_markdown` hook: find `@emgithub(file:label)` patterns, resolve via scanner, emit `<script>` tags
3. Pilot on Scalar fields page: add labels to source, convert 14 existing embeds, verify output
title: Dynamic code labeling for emgithub documentation

description:
## Research Question
Can we add a labeling system to source code so that documentation references code by label name rather than fragile line numbers? Research existing tools and whether we need a custom implementation.

## Summary
This pattern (label regions in source, reference by name in docs, resolve at build time) is well-established across many documentation systems. **PyMdown Snippets** is the most natural fit since we already use MkDocs + pymdownx extensions. However, no existing tool generates emgithub-style `<script>` embeds from named labels — that would require a small custom plugin.

## Key Findings

### Existing Tools That Do Exactly This

| Tool | Ecosystem | Label Syntax | Doc Reference | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **PyMdown Snippets** | MkDocs/pymdownx | `// --8<-- [start:name]` | `--8<-- "file:name"` | Best fit — same ecosystem we use |
| mdBook | Rust | `// ANCHOR: name` | `{{#include file:name}}` | Popular, clean syntax |
| VitePress | Vue | `// #region name` | `<<< @/file#name` | VS Code folding-aware |
| AsciiDoc | Antora | `// tag::name[]` | `include::file[tag=name]` | Most powerful filtering |
| Sphinx | RST | free-form markers | `:start-after:` / `:end-before:` | Oldest, most mature |
| MarkdownSnippets | .NET pre-processor | `// begin-snippet: name` | `snippet: name` | Only tool that also generates GitHub `#L` permalinks |

### PyMdown Snippets — Best Native Fit

Already part of the pymdownx ecosystem we use (`pymdownx.arithmatex`, `pymdownx.superfences`, `pymdownx.highlight` are all configured). Adding `pymdownx.snippets` to `mkdocs.yml` is trivial.

**Source code:**
```cpp
// --8<-- [start:model_params]
double lambda = 0.1;
double phi0 = 1.0;
// --8<-- [end:model_params]
```

**Documentation markdown:**
````markdown
```cpp
--8<-- "src/models/lphi4.h:model_params"
```
````

**Trade-off:** Inlines code at build time (rendered by Pygments). Loses the emgithub look (GitHub-style file header, "View on GitHub" link, jsDelivr fetch). Gains stability — labels move with the code, no line numbers to maintain.

### Custom Plugin Option — Keep emgithub Look

No existing tool generates emgithub `<script>` tags from named labels. A custom MkDocs hook or plugin would:

1. Scan source files for label markers (e.g., `// @label:name` ... `// @endlabel`)
2. Record the line ranges per label
3. In a markdown preprocessor, replace `@showcode path/to/file:name` with the emgithub `<script>` tag using resolved `#Lstart-Lend`

This could be implemented as:
- A `mkdocs-gen-files` script (we already use this for `exclusions.py`)
- A custom MkDocs hook (`on_page_markdown` event)
- A pymdownx inline processor

Estimated complexity: ~100-150 lines of Python.

### Hybrid Approach — Best of Both Worlds

Use PyMdown Snippets for **inlining code** (stable, well-tested) but add a companion link/button that points to the GitHub source. This avoids maintaining a custom plugin while keeping the "View on GitHub" affordance.

## Architecture Context

- Build system: MkDocs + Material theme (`documentation/source/mkdocs.yml`)
- Current embeds: 14 emgithub `<script>` tags in one page, with ~63 more to convert across 4 remaining phases
- Existing pymdownx extensions: `arithmatex`, `superfences`, `highlight`, `details`
- Custom JS/CSS already handles emgithub isolation (`emgithub-fixraw.js`, `extra.css`)
- Build script: `documentation/build.sh` clones source repos into `tmp/code_source/`

## Code References
- `documentation/source/mkdocs.yml` — MkDocs config, plugins and extensions
- `documentation/source/docs/Manual/My first model of (singlet) scalar fields.md` — page with 14 emgithub embeds
- `documentation/source/docs/javascripts/emgithub-fixraw.js` — custom emgithub post-processing
- `documentation/source/docs/extra.css:5-45` — emgithub isolation CSS
- `documentation/build.sh` — build pipeline, clones source repos
- `documentation/setup_python.sh` — Python venv setup, installs pymdownx

## Open Questions
1. Do we want to keep the emgithub visual style (GitHub file header, "View on GitHub" link) or is Pygments-rendered code acceptable?
2. Should labels live in the public `cosmolattice/cosmolattice` repo or the private one? (emgithub targets the public repo)
3. How should the build resolve labels if source files are cloned at build time into `tmp/code_source/`?
title: Research: Dynamic code labeling for documentation
